The Poison:
Exaggerating opponents' national ambitions and ideological ties inflames division to drive campaign donations.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing local representation (WHO) with national ideological caricature (WHAT), substituting sensational labels for substantive records.

Social Physics Analysis:
By casting opponents as radical extremists, candidates protect their turf through projection rather than engaging on policy outcomes.

The Unavoidable Truth: Campaigns frequently use hyperbole to energize partisan bases.

The Unavoidable Lie: Labeling opponents as radical puppets captures the full nuance of public service.
